title: Harness selection and execution
intro: First-release design, pending independent review. These are source-package and process views, not deployment containers. Graphs begin at a dark Start here node; sequence views begin at the first message.

groups.title: Package boundary
groups.description: One public command, an installed private worker, optional caller adapters.

groups.title: Execution and authority
groups.description: Selection ends before the foreground process becomes the harness.

groups.title: Original creator and review
groups.description: Artifact identity and observed evidence outlive mutable task paths.

discussion.title: Bounded policy evaluation followed by exec
discussion.summary: Rust owns admission and durable receipts. A compiled Bun worker evaluates explicitly selected TypeScript without completion authority. Provider separation remains in the supplied policy. Creator registration distinguishes recorded execution from owner declarations.

updatedDiagrams.summary: Assigned generic launch responsibilities to Rust and programmable selection to a private compiled worker.
Made record persistence and worker cleanup precede the final exec handoff.
Made original-creator registration explicit and same-provider choices refuse without fallback.

diagrams.title: Caller, dispatcher and policy packages
diagrams.caption: Source packages and runtime participants. Grove-specific relationship parsing belongs to the optional adapter; the generic command has no review-kind list.

diagrams.title: Prepare, record and replace the foreground process
diagrams.caption: The worker shares the enclosing job and receives no interactive stdin. Cancellation or timeout before admission launches nothing. Post-exec measurements require an external observer.

diagrams.title: Resolve one creator before selecting a reviewer
diagrams.caption: The policy owns provider comparison. A receipt of an attempted exec alone is insufficient for recorded creator registration; the owner can instead make an explicit declaration. Re-invocations preserve the existing creator association.
